hypothesis: L2 evict-first streaming loads in the split-KV decode kernel: the K and V tile loads in _attn_fwd_split get eviction_policy="evict_first" (read exactly once per call), so streamed KV lines replace each other in L2 instead of evicting the dirty lines left by do_bench's 256 MB zero-fill flush (which must then be written back to DRAM inside the timed window). Making the hint real requires launching the split kernel with num_stages=1: on the num_stages=2 cp.async path Triton drops the policy (cached PTX: plain cp.async.cg, no cache_hint). With num_stages=1 the PTX has ld.global.L1::evict_first.L2::cache_hint plus createpolicy.fractional.L2::evict_first. Split sizing, tiles, warps, combine kernel and the prefill path are unchanged.
rationale: Decode is DRAM-bound and the 16k-64k rows are the thinnest vs FA2 (~1.02-1.04x). Fitting measured decode times (HEAD, exp 8) to T = a + (read + writeback)/BW, with writeback = f * min(read, 96 MiB), gives a consistent fit: BW ~1.68 TB/s, a ~7.3 us (matching the small-decode overhead) and f ~0.16, i.e. ~10-15 MB of dirty flush lines written back during each 16k+ decode. A read-only fit instead needs the overhead to grow from 7 to 13 us with no clear cause. Evict-first for read-once data is the standard streaming hint. It is new: exps 7, 8, 10, 11 and 17 changed split sizing, tile or order, never the cache policy. Side effect, stated honestly: num_stages=1 drops split-kernel smem from 38.9 KB to 22.5 KB (cached JSON), so 4 CTAs/SM instead of 2. The 32k grid (592 CTAs) then runs in one wave, which resembles exp 17's residency change (that one used BLOCK_N=32 and gave 32k/64k -2/-4 us, 16k +1.7 us). The loads are now register loads instead of the single-buffered cp.async (exp 17 notes), so per-CTA latency hiding is roughly unchanged.
expected_effect: decode_16384/32768/65536 a few us faster each (from fewer writebacks plus the one-wave residency), small decodes about the same, prefill unchanged. If the L2 already cleans dirty lines eagerly, any change comes only from the 4-CTA/SM residency.
